How do I apply for a fertilizer license? Submit an application in Form A or A1 (for retail/industrial dealers) to the Controller of Fertilizers in your state, along with the prescribed fee (e.g., ?750 for retail, ?2250 for wholesale in Odisha) and a certificate of source in Form O. Documents like identity proof, business registration, and land records are required. Some states, like Odisha, offer online applications via portals like e-Licensing. What are the educational qualifications required for a fertilizer license? For a retail fertilizer license, applicants need qualifications like B.Sc. (Agriculture), B.Sc. (Chemistry), a Diploma in Agricultural Science, or a certificate course (minimum 6 months) from institutes like the National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management. Existing license holders before July 30, 2018, may be exempt from this for renewals. What is the validity and renewal process for a fertilizer license? The validity period varies by state, typically three years. For renewal, submit an application before expiry with the required fee and updated documents. Late renewals may incur penalties (e.g., ?60-75 in Odisha). Failure to renew can lead to license cancellation or the need to apply for a new one.

In India, whether you are a retailer, a wholesaler, or a manufacturer, getting a fertilizer license is a statutory requirement. Services Plus provides vast support for fertilizer license registration in India along with documentation, legal compliance, and follow-ups to ensure a fast and hassle-free registration process.
With full disclosure, timely work delivery, and all-round regulatory support, we are a well-stereotyped fertilizer license registration company in India.

A fertilizer license is a government-issued permit authorizing individuals or businesses to manufacture, sell, import, export, or distribute fertilizers in India. This license, issued under the Fertilizer (Control) Order, 1985, by the Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, maintains the guaranteed supply of standard-quality fertilizers to the farmers/agricultural market.
Fertilizer license registration in India typically falls into any one of the three categories:
1️. Retail Fertilizer License
A commercial fertilizer license enables a company to market fertilizers but not sell directly to consumers, such as the farmer, farmer's cooperative, and nursery.
Intended for home and garden supply for farmers and small landowners.
Holders should typically be qualified to at least the HND level in an agriculture orscience-related field (e.g., B.Sc. in agriculture or chemistry).
Needs a dedicated shop/storage area compliant with safety/handling standards.
Agricultural fertilizer shop license, which is most common.
Rural/agricultural individual entrepreneurship
Franchisee of agri-brand outlet
2️. Wholesale Fertilizer License
An agricultural fertilizer license is issued to individuals or corporations that want to sell fertilizers to other retailers, bulk buyers, or distributors.
Its bulk purchase and distribution of fertilizers.

How do I apply for a fertilizer license?

Submit an application in Form A or A1 (for retail/industrial dealers) to the Controller of Fertilizers in your state, along with the prescribed fee (e.g., ?750 for retail, ?2250 for wholesale in Odisha) and a certificate of source in Form O. Documents like identity proof, business registration, and land records are required. Some states, like Odisha, offer online applications via portals like e-Licensing.
What are the educational qualifications required for a fertilizer license?

For a retail fertilizer license, applicants need qualifications like B.Sc. (Agriculture), B.Sc. (Chemistry), a Diploma in Agricultural Science, or a certificate course (minimum 6 months) from institutes like the National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management. Existing license holders before July 30, 2018, may be exempt from this for renewals.
What is the validity and renewal process for a fertilizer license?

The validity period varies by state, typically three years. For renewal, submit an application before expiry with the required fee and updated documents. Late renewals may incur penalties (e.g., ?60-75 in Odisha). Failure to renew can lead to license cancellation or the need to apply for a new one.
